title: Cannabis Turkey Pot Pie with a Cannabutter Filling
h1: Turkey Pot Pie with Cannabutter in the Filling
metaDescription: A cozy cannabis turkey pot pie with cannabutter in the filling, cut into four even slices, plus low-heat tips that help protect your infusion's potency.

body:
A cannabis turkey pot pie is cannabis comfort food for fall, with a measured infusion. Cannabutter goes into the vegetables over low heat, the filling gets a thorough stir, and the pie is cut into four even slices, so each one carries a similar dose. Ready-made crusts and canned cream soup keep it simple, and leftover holiday turkey fits right in.

## How to dose a cannabis turkey pot pie

The math is short: total THC in the cannabutter you use, divided by 4, is the estimated dose per slice. Even mixing is what makes that true for every slice. Melt the cannabutter completely, fold the filling until the sauce looks uniform, and score four equal wedges in the top crust before baking.

Want a gentler slice? Use less [cannabutter](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/) and make up the difference with plain butter, rather than cutting smaller pieces. For scale, Michigan caps a store-bought adult-use edible at 10 mg THC per dose, as of October 2026. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) covers starting low.

## What goes in the filling

Diced cooked turkey, frozen mixed vegetables, celery, onion and a parboiled potato make the base. Two cans of condensed cream soup and a splash of milk become the sauce, and two refrigerated pie crusts with an egg wash finish it. Canna-oil can stand in for cannabutter. Starting from flower? Browse your nearest High Society store's [menu](/shop/) and order ahead for in-store or curbside pickup.

## The steps that matter most

Blind-bake the bottom crust briefly so it stays crisp. Keep the skillet on low while the vegetables soften in the cannabutter: a gentle sizzle, never browning. Then bake until the top is golden and the filling bubbles at the vents.

## Storing and labeling leftovers

Refrigerate leftovers within two hours in a container labeled 'contains THC', with the date and dose per slice. They keep 3 to 4 days. Reheat slices until the center reaches 165 °F. If anyone eats a slice by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

Serve this pie only to adults 21+ who know exactly what's in it, like the guests at a [Friendsgiving for adults who partake](/blog/cannabis-friendsgiving-essentials/). A family table, where someone could take a slice unaware, is the wrong place for it. Find more ideas in our [holiday infused recipes](/blog/holiday-cannabis-infused-recipes/).

## Variations

- **Chicken:** same method, with cooked chicken in place of turkey.
- **Puff-pastry lid:** skip the bottom crust, bake the filling in a dish and top it with puff pastry.
- **From-scratch sauce:** skip the soup and stir 3 tablespoons of flour into the softened vegetables. Whisk in 1 1/2 cups broth and 1/2 cup milk, then simmer gently until thick.

Enjoy it responsibly, and keep it 21+.

faq.q: Can I use leftover Thanksgiving turkey?
faq.a: Yes, it's an ideal use for it. Dice or shred about 3 cups and skip the cooking step. Use turkey that went into the fridge within two hours of the meal and is no more than 3 to 4 days old. Bake until the center of the pie reaches 165 °F.

faq.q: Will baking reduce the THC in the filling?
faq.a: Some THC can be lost whenever heat runs long, but a pie is fairly gentle. The moist filling stays near the boiling point of water even in a 375 °F oven. The bigger risk comes earlier, from browning the cannabutter or leaving it on high heat, so keep the sauté low and slow.

faq.q: Can I freeze infused pot pie?
faq.a: Yes. Freeze the cooled pie whole or by the slice, wrapped tightly and labeled with the dose per slice and the date, and use it within 3 to 4 months. Thaw it in the fridge overnight, then reheat it in the oven until the center reaches 165 °F.

ingredients: 3 cups cooked turkey, diced or shredded (or 1 1/4 pounds raw turkey breast)
3 tablespoons fat for the vegetables: your measured cannabutter or canna-oil, plus plain butter to make up the rest (see the dosing note)
1 medium potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes and parboiled for 5 minutes
2 cans (10.5 ounces each) condensed cream of chicken or cream of mushroom soup
1/2 teaspoon dried thyme, plus salt and pepper
steps: If you are starting with raw turkey breast, poach or roast it until it reaches 165 °F inside, then cool and dice it.
Heat the oven to 400 °F. Press one crust into a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate, dock the base with a fork in a dozen places and bake for 8 to 10 minutes. Turn the oven down to 375 °F.
Melt the cannabutter and plain butter in a wide skillet over low heat. Add the onion, celery and potato and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until soft but not browned.
Take the skillet off the heat. Fold in the turkey, mixed vegetables, soup, milk and seasonings until the sauce looks uniform.
Spoon the filling into the crust and level it. Cover with the second crust, crimp the edges, cut four vents and brush with the egg wash.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until deep golden with filling bubbling at the vents. Rest 15 minutes, then cut 4 equal slices.
recipe.dosingNote: **Per-slice estimate:** total THC in the cannabutter you use ÷ 4 slices. Example: if the cannabutter you add carries about 20 mg THC in total, each slice holds roughly 5 mg, provided the filling is well mixed. Homemade cannabutter varies with the potency of the flower and with losses during decarboxylation and infusion, so the figure is only an estimate. Eat one slice and wait at least 2 hours before more. Label leftovers, and keep the pie away from children and pets.

sources.label: University of Illinois Extension: Leftovers (food safety)
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency: Technical Bulletin, Maximum THC Concentrations for Marijuana-Infused Products (April 24, 2025)
Wang M. et al. (2016), Decarboxylation study of acidic cannabinoids, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research

review.summary: 16 claims checked: 16 ok (one law sentence's wording aligned to law-facts). Nothing wrong, unsupported or overstated found.

claims.claim: Dose per slice = total THC in the cannabutter ÷ 4; example about 20 mg ÷ 4 = roughly 5 mg, as an estimate
claims.source: arithmetic (20 ÷ 4 = 5); stated as an example, not a fixed figure, per the brief

claims.claim: Homemade cannabutter varies with flower potency and decarboxylation and infusion losses (dosing note)
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST): 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: Michigan caps a store-bought adult-use edible at 10 mg THC per serving, as of October 2026
claims.fix: 'per serving' became 'per dose' to match the law-facts plain claim word for word; 'as of October 2026' kept
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-thc-limits: 'Adult-use edibles in Michigan are capped at 10 mg THC per dose and 200 mg per package' (CRA technical bulletin, April 24, 2025, already in the sources list; michigan.gov not re-opened, per instructions)

claims.claim: Some THC can be lost whenever heat runs long (FAQ)
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/, reviewing earlier work: THC peaked 'in ∼5–10 min at 145°C followed by a significant loss at longer times possibly due to evaporation'

claims.claim: In the oven the moist filling stays near the boiling point of water, far below a 375 °F dial setting (takeaway, FAQ)
claims.source: general physics, not separately sourced: water boils at about 212 °F at sea level and a wet filling does not climb past its boiling point while water remains (the recipe's doneness cue is the filling bubbling at the vents); usgs.gov timed out from this machine

claims.claim: The bigger THC risk is browning the cannabutter or leaving it on high heat, so keep the sauté low (FAQ, steps)
claims.source: reasoning: butter only browns once its water is gone and the fat runs hotter than boiling; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ reports losses at 145 °C and CBN formation 'at 160°C and 180°C' in the studies it reviews

claims.claim: Refrigerate leftovers within two hours; they keep 3 to 4 days; reheat to 165 °F (body, takeaway, FAQ)
claims.source: https://extension.illinois.edu/food-safety/leftovers (WebFetch): 'Leftover food should be refrigerated or frozen within two hours of serving.'; 'Use refrigerated leftover food within 3-4 days'; 'reheat to a minimum of 165 F'

claims.claim: Frozen infused pie: use within 3 to 4 months; thaw in the fridge, reheat until the center reaches 165 °F
claims.source: https://extension.illinois.edu/food-safety/leftovers: 'within 3 to 4 months if they were frozen'; 'reheat to a minimum of 165 F'

claims.claim: Raw turkey breast: cook until it reaches 165 °F inside (step 1)
claims.source: https://extension.illinois.edu/turkey/using-meat-thermometer (WebFetch): 'turkeys and turkey parts are safe when cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165 °F' (fsis.usda.gov and foodsafety.gov return 403 here)

claims.claim: Leftover holiday turkey: use turkey refrigerated within two hours and no more than 3 to 4 days old (FAQ)
Two 10.5-ounce cans of condensed cream soup
claims.source: WebSearch 2026-10-24: retailers list condensed cream of chicken soup in the standard '10.5 oz Can' (no brand named in the article)

claims.claim: Bake times: crust blind-baked 8 to 10 minutes at 400 °F, then 30 to 35 minutes at 375 °F (cook time 45 minutes)
claims.source: internal consistency: 8-10 + 30-35 minutes = 38-45 minutes, matching cookTime; ordinary pot-pie technique, no safety figure

claims.claim: If anyone eats a slice by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'

claims.claim: Eat one slice and wait at least 2 hours before more; keep the pie away from children and pets
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'; 'Infants or young children who unintentionally ingest cannabis are more likely to require hospital admission'

claims.claim: High Society: browse your nearest store's menu and order ahead for in-store or curbside pickup
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering (online order for pickup), services.inStorePickup ('In-store pickup and in-store shopping at every store'), services.curbside ('offered at every store'); no product named as stocked

claims.claim: Serve only to adults 21+ who know it is infused, never at a mixed family table; keep it 21+
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-age (adult-use law covers 21+ only); brief mustAvoid (mixed holiday table)

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. Food-safety figures checked against two Illinois Extension pages (federal food-safety hosts refuse this machine); onset and Poison Control against the CDC FAQ; the heat claims against Wang 2016 read in full (its 145 °C figure reviews earlier work and is cited here as such). The one law sentence matches law-facts mi-thc-limits and keeps 'as of October 2026'. Sources list kept: all four are https, exist and support the text. High Society: one mention (menu, order ahead, in-store or curbside pickup), all in hs-facts; no prices, phones, hours, app, staff or stocked products. Writer's notes: Mixed holiday table explicitly discouraged (brief mustAvoid). No brand, no named staff, example mg only. High Society mentioned once (menu, in-store or curbside pickup).
